9:1.sourceText: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἰσίν τινες ὧδε τῶν ἑστηκότων οἵτινες οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου ἕως ἂν ἴδωσιν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐληλυθυῖαν ἐν δυνάμει.
9:1.targetText: Then Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, there are some standing here who will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God arrive with power.”

groups.note: τῶν ἑστηκότων ("of those standing") is rendered standing.
οὐ μή is an emphatic double negative.
The aorist subjunctive under οὐ μή is rendered as an English future.
ἕως ἄν ("until") is rendered before.

unmappedSource.reason: The ὅτι introducing the saying is not rendered in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker that the Greek verb ending implies.

9:2.sourceText: Καὶ μετὰ ἡμέρας ἓξ παραλαμβάνει ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τὸν Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάνην, καὶ ἀναφέρει αὐτοὺς εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν κατ’ ἰδίαν μόνους. καὶ μετεμορφώθη ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν,
9:2.targetText: After six days Jesus took with Him Peter, James, and John, and led them up a high mountain by themselves. There He was transfigured before them.

groups.note: ἀναφέρει … εἰς ("brings up onto") is rendered led … up.
κατ’ ἰδίαν μόνους ("privately, alone") is rendered by themselves.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the verse-opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB lists the names with a comma; this καί is not separately expressed.
BSB starts a new sentence here, so this καί is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the place word (the mountain); the Greek has no locative adverb, as in Matthew 17:2.

9:3.sourceText: καὶ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο στίλβοντα λευκὰ λίαν, οἷα γναφεὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς οὐ δύναται οὕτως λευκᾶναι.
9:3.targetText: His clothes became radiantly white, brighter than any launderer on earth could bleach them.

groups.note: στίλβοντα … λίαν ("glistening … exceedingly") is rendered radiantly.
οἷα … οὕτως ("such as … so") is recast as brighter than; οἷα, the object of λευκᾶναι, is rendered them.
"Such as no launderer could" is recast as "than any launderer could", so the negative οὐ becomes any.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the verse-opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

9:4.sourceText: καὶ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς Ἡλείας σὺν Μωϋσεῖ, καὶ ἦσαν συνλαλοῦντες τῷ Ἰησοῦ.
9:4.targetText: And Elijah and Moses appeared before them, talking with Jesus.

groups.note: σύν ("with") joins the two names and is rendered and.
The periphrastic ἦσαν συνλαλοῦντες ("were talking with") is rendered talking with.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders the second clause as a participle phrase, so this καί has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

groups.note: The answering participle ἀποκριθείς and λέγει are condensed to said.

The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

groups.note: The second γάρ ("for") is recast as the result frame so … that.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject that the Greek verb ending implies.
English idiom; the Greek has only τί (what).

9:12.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτοῖς Ἡλείας μὲν ἐλθὼν πρῶτον ἀποκαθιστάνει πάντα· καὶ πῶς γέγραπται ἐπὶ τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἵνα πολλὰ πάθῃ καὶ ἐξουδενηθῇ;

9:37.sourceText: Ὃς ἂν ἓν τῶν τοιούτων παιδίων δέξηται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου, ἐμὲ δέχεται· καὶ ὃς ἂν ἐμὲ δέχηται, οὐκ ἐμὲ δέχεται ἀλλὰ τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.
9:37.targetText: “Whoever welcomes one of these little children in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes not only Me, but the One who sent Me.”

groups.note: τοιούτων ("such") is rendered these.
The article with the participle, "the one having sent", is rendered the One who sent.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds only to soften not … but; the Greek has no word for it.

9:38.sourceText: Ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰωάνης Διδάσκαλε, εἴδομέν τινα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ἐκβάλλοντα δαιμόνια, ὃς οὐκ ἀκολουθεῖ ἡμῖν, καὶ ἐκωλύομεν αὐτόν, ὅτι οὐκ ἠκολούθει ἡμῖν.
9:38.targetText: John said to Him, “Teacher, we saw someone else driving out demons in Your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not accompany us.”

groups.note: The imperfect ἐκωλύομεν ("we were hindering") is rendered as an attempt.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
ὃς οὐκ ἀκολουθεῖ ἡμῖν ("who does not follow us"): BSB renders the repeated clause only once, in the ὅτι clause.

unmappedTarget.reason: English idiom; the Greek has only τινα (someone).

9:39.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Μὴ κωλύετε αὐτόν· οὐδεὶς γάρ ἐστιν ὃς ποιήσει δύναμιν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου καὶ δυνήσεται ταχὺ κακολογῆσαί με·
9:39.targetText: “Do not stop him,” Jesus replied. “For no one who performs a miracle in My name can turn around and speak evil of Me.

groups.note: ταχύ ("soon, quickly") is rendered with the English idiom turn around and.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
BSB renders "there is no one who" as no one who, so ἐστιν has no English word.
This καί joins ποιήσει and δυνήσεται; BSB makes can the main verb, so it is not expressed.

9:40.sourceText: ὃς γὰρ οὐκ ἔστιν καθ’ ἡμῶν, ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐστιν.
9:40.targetText: For whoever is not against us is for us.

9:41.sourceText: Ὃς γὰρ ἂν ποτίσῃ ὑμᾶς ποτήριον ὕδατος ἐν ὀνόματι, ὅτι Χριστοῦ ἐστε, ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ ἀπολέσῃ τὸν μισθὸν αὐτοῦ.
9:41.targetText: Indeed, if anyone gives you even a cup of water because you bear the name of Christ, truly I tell you, he will never lose his reward.

groups.note: The indefinite relative ὃς ἄν ("whoever") is rendered as a condition.
ἐν ὀνόματι ("in the name") is joined to the because-clause as bear the name of Christ.
ἐστε ("you are") with Χριστοῦ ("Christ's") is rendered you bear the name of Christ.
οὐ μή is an emphatic double negative.
The aorist subjunctive under οὐ μή is rendered as an English future.

unmappedSource.reason: The ὅτι introducing the saying is not rendered in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds even for emphasis; the Greek has no word for it.

9:42.sourceText: Καὶ ὃς ἂν σκανδαλίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων τῶν πιστευόντων, καλόν ἐστιν αὐτῷ μᾶλλον εἰ περίκειται μύλος ὀνικὸς περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ βέβληται εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν.
9:42.targetText: But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea.

groups.note: The indefinite relative ὃς ἄν ("whoever") is rendered as a condition.
καλόν … μᾶλλον ("good … rather") is rendered better.
The εἰ clause is rendered as an English infinitive.
The passive περίκειται ("is laid around") is rendered have … hung.
ὀνικός ("of a donkey") marks a millstone turned by a donkey, rendered large.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: N1904 has no εἰς ἐμέ after τῶν πιστευόντων; BSB's in Me matches the reading that includes it.

9:43.sourceText: Καὶ ἐὰν σκανδαλίσῃ σε ἡ χείρ σου, ἀπόκοψον αὐτήν· καλόν ἐστίν σε κυλλὸν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν, ἢ τὰς δύο χεῖρας ἔχοντα ἀπελθεῖν εἰς τὴν γέενναν, εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ ἄσβεστον.
9:43.targetText: If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life crippled than to have two hands and go into hell, into the unquenchable fire.

groups.note: σκανδαλίσῃ ("causes to stumble") is rendered causes … to sin.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the verse-opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The preposition repeats the verb's prefix and is absorbed in English enter.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; Greek joins the participle ἔχοντα (having) to ἀπελθεῖν without a conjunction.

9:45.sourceText: καὶ ἐὰν ὁ πούς σου σκανδαλίζῃ σε, ἀπόκοψον αὐτόν· καλόν ἐστίν σε εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν χωλὸν, ἢ τοὺς δύο πόδας ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν γέενναν.
9:45.targetText: If your foot causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into hell.

The preposition repeats the verb's prefix and is absorbed in English enter.

9:47.sourceText: καὶ ἐὰν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου σκανδαλίζῃ σε, ἔκβαλε αὐτόν· καλόν σέ ἐστιν μονόφθαλμον εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἢ δύο ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν γέενναν,
9:47.targetText: And if your eye causes you to sin, pluck it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into hell,

The preposition repeats the verb's prefix and is absorbed in English enter.

9:48.sourceText: ὅπου ὁ σκώληξ αὐτῶν οὐ τελευτᾷ καὶ τὸ πῦρ οὐ σβέννυται.
9:48.targetText: where ‘their worm never dies, and the fire is never quenched.’

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

9:49.targetText: For everyone will be salted with fire.

9:50.sourceText: καλὸν τὸ ἅλας· ἐὰν δὲ τὸ ἅλας ἄναλον γένηται, ἐν τίνι αὐτὸ ἀρτύσετε; ἔχετε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἅλα καὶ εἰρηνεύετε ἐν ἀλλήλοις.
9:50.targetText: Salt is good, but if the salt loses its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt among yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”

groups.note: ἄναλον γένηται ("becomes saltless") is rendered loses its saltiness.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
